# P15 approve-reachability report: pn-workspace.toml marker as a trusted exec location (TrustedCheckoutExec)

Generated by `GeneratePnWorkspaceMarkerP15` (internal/effectpolicy/p15report.go) and pinned by
`TestP15ReportPnWorkspaceMarker`; regenerate with `go test ./internal/effectpolicy -run TestP15ReportPnWorkspaceMarker -update`.
Each row is one spec fact probed through the real engine (default registry and policies).

Change under review: `TrustedCheckoutExec` is Permitted when the working directory is inside a git or go checkout, and now ALSO when it is at or under a `pn-workspace.toml` (operator ruling, 2026-10-12). "inside" is a workforest set directory of a pn workspace that carries no git or go marker; "outside" is a directory with no marker above it, which is how every such directory behaved before the change. A fact is newly approved when it is approve inside and not approve outside.

What to check: the newly approved facts are ONLY Exec producers (one section per command path, listed by `ExecProducerPaths`), the same class `go test` already gets inside a git/go checkout; every control fact (no Exec fact, or an Exec fact the marker never reaches) has the same verdict inside and outside. `pn`/`pnwf` workspace-code verbs are Exec producers too: before the change they approved from any directory (inert-literal model), so for them the net effect against the previous behavior is a narrowing outside a marker, and no change inside.
